trials.notes: Used the correct tree-aware processor, only documented methods, and the canonical breadcrumb pattern: exclude the current node, look for UL/OL ancestors, mutate with add_class(), and return get_updated_html(). Passed 7/7 with no _doing_it_wrong records.

Correct processor and all method calls are documented. The next_token() loop with get_token_type()/is_tag_closer() is valid, though broader than necessary for opener-only tag mutation where next_tag() would be simpler. Passed 7/7 with no _doing_it_wrong records.

Correct processor and documented methods throughout. The is_tag_closer() guard after plain next_tag() is redundant because next_tag() skips closers by default, but harmless. Passed 7/7 with no _doing_it_wrong records.

failure_analysis: All trials passed every frozen case: simple nested OL-in-UL, top-level lists, UL-in-OL, deep descendant, existing class preservation, multiple nested levels, and mixed document. The docs succeeded on the key concepts: the processor-selection guidance explicitly says to use WP_HTML_Processor when structure or containment matters; the breadcrumbs section explains that get_breadcrumbs() returns the stack down to the current node; add_class() documents class preservation/appending; and get_updated_html() documents byte preservation for untouched input. The main near-misses were not functional failures: trial-2 used a full token walk for an opener-only edit, and trial-3 defensively checked is_tag_closer() after next_tag() despite the documented default closer-skipping behavior.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs say breadcrumbs include the current node, but they do not give a compact idiom for testing ancestors without accidentally counting the current element itself.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a general note: for an ancestor-only test, inspect all breadcrumbs except the final item; the direct parent is the second-to-last item, and implicit HTML/BODY entries may appear before source elements.

doc_gaps.problem: The closer-skipping default is documented in the parameter table, but it is easy to miss in task-oriented examples, leading to redundant is_tag_closer() checks or unnecessarily broad next_token() loops.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short tag-only traversal recipe showing plain next_tag() for opener mutations, and reserve tag_closers => 'visit' or next_token() for cases that actually need closers, text, comments, or other token types.

doc_gaps.location: html-processor.md > HTML Support / get_updated_html() inherited mutation behavior
doc_gaps.problem: The docs explain unsupported markup and incomplete input policies for parsing and serialization, but are less explicit about what callers should do when returning get_updated_html() after queued class/attribute mutations if the processor later aborts or pauses.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Clarify the contract for class/attribute mutations after get_last_error() or paused_at_incomplete_token(): whether queued updates are applied, whether untouched bytes remain preserved, and when callers should fail closed or return the original input.
